subject: English
passage: European honeybees typically have golden-brown coloring, but some members of the species have a version of a gene, or gene variant, that gives them a darker, almost black appearance instead. Heather Wakefield and her team studied fifteen honeybee colonies across different regions. They found that the dark-colored bees are more common in areas where Varroa mite infestations occur frequently. The team also discovered that the dark-colored bees are more likely to resist Varroa mite damage than the golden-brown bees are. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: European honeybees face more severe mite infestations than other bee species do.
choices.B: the honey production levels of bee colonies are likely to improve over time because of a particular gene variant.
choices.C: dark-colored bees will soon replace golden-brown bees across Europe.
choices.D: the gene variant that results in dark coloring may be linked to resistance to Varroa mites.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The text tells us that the dark-colored bees are more common in areas with frequent Varroa mite infestations and are more likely to resist mite damage than the golden-brown bees. This suggests that the gene variant that results in dark coloring may be linked to resistance to Varroa mites.
